The current/canonical implementation lives in `NebulaPluginNova/Modules/NebulaRPC.cs` (≈1100 lines).

### 1. How Nebula defines custom RPC IDs
Custom methods are turned into RPCs via the `[NebulaRPC]` attribute (defined in `NebulaAPI/Attributes/NebulaAttribute.cs:11`):
```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method)]
[RequiringHandshake]
public class NebulaRPC : Attribute { }
```
- It is a **method-level** attribute (not the Reactor `[MethodRpc]` style — it replaces the whole method body with an RPC call).
- `[NebulaRPCHolder]` marks a class whose methods should be scanned for `[NebulaRPC]` methods.
- RPC IDs are **string-hash based**, not numeric enums. `RemoteProcessBase` computes `Hash = name.ComputeConstantHash()`, stored in `Dictionary<int, RemoteProcessBase> AllNebulaProcess`. The legacy version (`Nebula/Rpc/NebulaRPC.cs`) used a manual prime-multiply hash (`MulPrime=127`, `SurPrime=104729`).

### 2. How they send RPCs
Two layers:

**Low-level sending** — `RPCRouter.SendRpc(...)` and `RPCRouter.SendDummy(...)` in `NebulaPluginNova/Modules/NebulaRPC.cs`. This is the core of the network write:

var origWriter = AmongUsLLImpl.AmongUsClientInstance.StartRpcImmediately(AmongUsLLImpl.LocalPlayer.NetId, 128, shouldBeReliable ? Hazel.SendOption.Reliable : Hazel.SendOption.None, -1);
var virialWriter = MessageWriter.Get();
virialWriter.Write(hash);
sender.Invoke(virialWriter);
virialWriter.End(origWriter);
AmongUsLLImpl.AmongUsClientInstance.FinishRpcImmediately(origWriter);
```

- `RemoteProcess<Parameter>.Invoke` / `RemoteProcess.Invoke()` / `DivisibleRemoteProcess.Invoke` / `LongRemoteProcess` all funnel through `RPCRouter.SendRpc`.
- `LongRemoteProcess` splits large payloads into 800-byte packets with a cache ID header (`id, length, num, index, bytes`).
- `NebulaRPCInvoker` is a deferred/schedulable send handle with `InvokeSingle()`, `InvokeLocal()`, and `IsDummy` support.

static void Postfix(byte callId, Hazel.MessageReader reader) {
    if (callId != 128) return;
    ReceiveMessage(reader);

I now have a complete picture of the custom RPC/Remote invocation system. Let me compile my findings.

## Findings: Nebula Custom RPC/Remote Invocation System

I identified and fully read the entire custom RPC system. There are **two generations** of the system—the legacy one in `Nebula/Rpc/NebulaRPC.cs` and the current one in `NebulaPluginNova/Modules/NebulaRPC.cs`. The current/canonical implementation lives in `NebulaPluginNova/Modules/NebulaRPC.cs` (≈1100 lines).

### 1. How Nebula defines custom RPC IDs
Custom methods are turned into RPCs via the `[NebulaRPC]` attribute (defined in `NebulaAPI/Attributes/NebulaAttribute.cs:11`):
```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method)]
[RequiringHandshake]
public class NebulaRPC : Attribute { }
```
- It is a **method-level** attribute (not the Reactor `[MethodRpc]` style — it replaces the whole method body with an RPC call).
- `[NebulaRPCHolder]` marks a class whose methods should be scanned for `[NebulaRPC]` methods.
- RPC IDs are **string-hash based**, not numeric enums. `RemoteProcessBase` computes `Hash = name.ComputeConstantHash()`, stored in `Dictionary<int, RemoteProcessBase> AllNebulaProcess`. The legacy version (`Nebula/Rpc/NebulaRPC.cs`) used a manual prime-multiply hash (`MulPrime=127`, `SurPrime=104729`).

### 2. How they send RPCs
Two layers:

**Low-level sending** — `RPCRouter.SendRpc(...)` and `RPCRouter.SendDummy(...)` in `NebulaPluginNova/Modules/NebulaRPC.cs`. This is the core of the network write:
```csharp
var origWriter = AmongUsLLImpl.AmongUsClientInstance.StartRpcImmediately(AmongUsLLImpl.LocalPlayer.NetId, 128, shouldBeReliable ? Hazel.SendOption.Reliable : Hazel.SendOption.None, -1);
var virialWriter = MessageWriter.Get();
virialWriter.Write(hash);
sender.Invoke(virialWriter);
virialWriter.End(origWriter);
AmongUsLLImpl.AmongUsClientInstance.FinishRpcImmediately(origWriter);
```
- **callId `128`** is the custom RPC channel (the legacy version used `64`).
- `RemoteProcess<Parameter>.Invoke` / `RemoteProcess.Invoke()` / `DivisibleRemoteProcess.Invoke` / `LongRemoteProcess` all funnel through `RPCRouter.SendRpc`.
- `LongRemoteProcess` splits large payloads into 800-byte packets with a cache ID header (`id, length, num, index, bytes`).
- `NebulaRPCInvoker` is a deferred/schedulable send handle with `InvokeSingle()`, `InvokeLocal()`, and `IsDummy` support.

**Batching/RPC Sections** — `RPCRouter.CreateSection()` / `RPCSection` (exposed publicly as `NebulaAPI.CreateRPCSection(label)` in `NebulaAPI.cs:404`). RPCs issued inside a `using` section are buffered into `List<NebulaRPCInvoker> evacuateds` and flushed together via `CombinedRemoteProcess.CombinedRPC.Invoke(...)`, guaranteeing all clients execute them simultaneously in the same order.

### 3. How they receive and handle RPCs
`NebulaRPCInGameHandlerPatch` (also `NebulaRPCHandlerPatch` in legacy) is a Harmony postfix on `PlayerControl.HandleRpc`:
```csharp
static void Postfix(byte callId, Hazel.MessageReader reader) {
    if (callId != 128) return;
    ReceiveMessage(reader);
}
```
`ReceiveMessage` wraps the reader, reads the int hash id, looks it up in `AllNebulaProcess`, then calls `rpc.Receive(virialReadaer)`. `RemoteProcess.Receive` deserializes parameters via the receiver function and invokes `Body.Invoke(parameter, false)`.

### 4. The full RPC invoke pattern
- **`[NebulaRPC]` method auto-transformation** — `RemoteProcessBase.WrapRpcMethod` (in the `NebulaPreprocess(FixStructure)` phase) Harmony-patches each `[NebulaRPC]` static method. It builds a `RemoteProcess<object[]>` whose sender/receiver serialize each method parameter via `RemoteProcessAsset.GetProcess(type)`, and the body calls the copied original. The prefix captures the args, invokes the RPC, and returns `false` (skips original). Addon assemblies with `[NebulaRPC]` methods are auto-marked `MarkAsNeedingHandshake()`.
- **Type serialization** — `RemoteProcessArgumentBase` / `RemoteProcessArgument<T>` register writers/readers for primitives (int, float, bool, string, byte, etc.), `Vector2/3/4`, `VVector`, `VColor`, `OutfitCandidate`, modulator types, `PlayerModInfo`, `GamePlayer`, `IPlayerlike`, `DeadBody`, achievements, `DefinedAssignable` roles, and `PlayerControl`.
- **`RemoteProcessAsset.GetProcess(type)`** handles arrays, tuples (`ITuple`), enums, and registered types dynamically.
- **`RemoteProcessArgumentsHelpers`** provides extension methods: `writer.Write<T>(obj)`, `reader.ReadCustom<T>()`, `WriteIfNotNullCustom`, `ReadIfNotNullCustom`.
- **`RemotePrimitiveProcess`** offers quick factories: `OfInteger`, `OfFloat`, `OfString`, `OfByte`, `OfVector2`, `OfVector3`.
- **`[NebulaRPCHolder]` classes** — `CombinedRemoteProcess` (batch section), `RoleRPC` (role-ability arg sync with per-ability `Definition`), `PropertyRPC` (request/reply property getter with timeouts), `RoleRPC.SyncRoleArgument`.
- **`QueryRPC.Generate<Q,A>`** creates a request/`Answer` RPC pair.
- **`RPCScheduler`** lets you defer `NebulaRPCInvoker`s to `PreMeeting`/`AfterMeeting` triggers, then flush via `CombinedRPC.Invoke`.

### 5. Public API surface (in `NebulaAPI全部源码.txt`)
- `NebulaAPI.CreateRPCSection(string?)` (L285/404) — the batch section entry point.
- `NebulaRPC` attribute (L2631) — method-to-RPC.
- `RegisterRpcType<T, V>(serializer, deserializer)` (L12327) — add a new RPC-serializable type.
- `TranslatableTag` (L12269) — RPC-transmittable text tags.
- Numerous "このAPIはRPCを送信します" (this API sends an RPC) comments around L10122–10324 (kill/win-related high-level RPC APIs).

### Key files
- `NebulaPluginNova/Modules/NebulaRPC.cs` — **the full current implementation** (RPCRouter, RemoteProcessBase, RemoteProcess<T>, LongRemoteProcess, DivisibleRemoteProcess, RemoteProcessAsset, RemoteProcessArgument, CombinedRemoteProcess, RoleRPC, PropertyRPC, RPCScheduler, handler patch).
- `Nebula/Rpc/NebulaRPC.cs` — legacy version (callId 64, prime-hash).
- `NebulaAPI/Attributes/NebulaAttribute.cs` — `[NebulaRPC]`, `[NebulaRPCHolder]` (via `[NebulaPreprocess]` scanning), `[RequiringHandshake]`.
- `NebulaAPI/NebulaAPI.cs` — public `CreateRPCSection` API.
- `NebulaAPI/Internal/AmongUsLL.cs` — low-level `AmongUsClientInstance`/`LocalPlayer` accessor.

I have thoroughly covered all requested search areas. The complete custom RPC system (ID hashing, sending via `RPCRouter`/callId 128, receiving via `HandleRpc` postfix, batching via `RPCSection`/`CombinedRemoteProcess`, and the `[NebulaRPC]` auto-transformation layer) is fully documented above.

# Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, and world generation capabilities.

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_world / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Generation Tools

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (tripo P1 default, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, rodin Gen-2.5 for high-quality tiers, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_world: text-to-world or image-to-world (World Labs Marble)
- generate_sound_effect / generate_music / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Sprite Animation

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot; Step 2 uses it as reference to produce a UI cutout sheet on magenta background for element extraction
- generate_sprite_atlas: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns result immediately, no polling)

## Findings: Nebula Custom RPC/Remote Invocation System

I identified and fully read the entire custom RPC system. There are **two generations** of the system—the legacy one in `Nebula/Rpc/NebulaRPC.cs` and the current one in `NebulaPluginNova/Modules/NebulaRPC.cs`. The current/canonical implementation lives in `NebulaPluginNova/Modules/NebulaRPC.cs` (≈1100 lines).

### 1. How Nebula defines custom RPC IDs
Custom methods are turned into RPCs via the `[NebulaRPC]` attribute (defined in `NebulaAPI/Attributes/NebulaAttribute.cs:11`):
```csharp
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method)]
[RequiringHandshake]
public class NebulaRPC : Attribute { }
```
- It is a **method-level** attribute (not the Reactor `[MethodRpc]` style — it replaces the whole method body with an RPC call).
- `[NebulaRPCHolder]` marks a class whose methods should be scanned for `[NebulaRPC]` methods.
- RPC IDs are **string-hash based**, not numeric enums. `RemoteProcessBase` computes `Hash = name.ComputeConstantHash()`, stored in `Dictionary<int, RemoteProcessBase> AllNebulaProcess`. The legacy version (`Nebula/Rpc/NebulaRPC.cs`) used a manual prime-multiply hash (`MulPrime=127`, `SurPrime=104729`).

### 2. How they send RPCs
Two layers:

**Low-level sending** — `RPCRouter.SendRpc(...)` and `RPCRouter.SendDummy(...)` in `NebulaPluginNova/Modules/NebulaRPC.cs`. This is the core of the network write:
```csharp
var origWriter = AmongUsLLImpl.AmongUsClientInstance.StartRpcImmediately(AmongUsLLImpl.LocalPlayer.NetId, 128, shouldBeReliable ? Hazel.SendOption.Reliable : Hazel.SendOption.None, -1);
var virialWriter = MessageWriter.Get();
virialWriter.Write(hash);
sender.Invoke(virialWriter);
virialWriter.End(origWriter);
AmongUsLLImpl.AmongUsClientInstance.FinishRpcImmediately(origWriter);
```
- **callId `128`** is the custom RPC channel (the legacy version used `64`).
- `RemoteProcess<Parameter>.Invoke` / `RemoteProcess.Invoke()` / `DivisibleRemoteProcess.Invoke` / `LongRemoteProcess` all funnel through `RPCRouter.SendRpc`.
- `LongRemoteProcess` splits large payloads into 800-byte packets with a cache ID header (`id, length, num, index, bytes`).
- `NebulaRPCInvoker` is a deferred/schedulable send handle with `InvokeSingle()`, `InvokeLocal()`, and `IsDummy` support.

**Batching/RPC Sections** — `RPCRouter.CreateSection()` / `RPCSection` (exposed publicly as `NebulaAPI.CreateRPCSection(label)` in `NebulaAPI.cs:404`). RPCs issued inside a `using` section are buffered into `List<NebulaRPCInvoker> evacuateds` and flushed together via `CombinedRemoteProcess.CombinedRPC.Invoke(...)`, guaranteeing all clients execute them simultaneously in the same order.

```csharp
static void Postfix(byte callId, Hazel.MessageReader reader) {

    ReceiveMessage(reader);
}
```

# Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, and world generation capabilities.

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_world / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Generation Tools

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (tripo P1 default, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, rodin Gen-2.5 for high-quality tiers, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_world: text-to-world or image-to-world (World Labs Marble)
- generate_sound_effect / generate_music / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Sprite Animation

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot; Step 2 uses it as reference to produce a UI cutout sheet on magenta background for element extraction
- generate_sprite_atlas: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns result immediately, no polling)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Rigging & Motion Tools

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async). Use check_task with the task_id to poll for completion.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
Poll check_task every 40s for 3D/video/world/rigging/motion tasks, every 10s for other tasks, until status is "completed" or "failed".
IMPORTANT: You MUST launch a background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to poll check_task at the recommended interval. Do NOT poll check_task directly in the foreground.
